title: How would you estimate how many smartphones are sold in India each year?
description: A step-by-step estimate for "How many smartphones are sold in India each year?" with the approach, the maths and a sanity check.
hook: Large populations make small assumptions matter a lot. Here, the ownership rate and how often people replace their phone do most of the work. Have a go at your own estimate before reading on.
body:
The question

How many smartphones are sold in India each year?

The approach

People × share with a smartphone ÷ years between replacements.

Tip: Before giving the answer, check it from a second direction. It is the step most candidates skip.

Step by step

  1. People in India: 1.4B
  2. × 50% own a smartphone
  3. ÷ 4 years before they replace it

That gives about 175M phones a year.

Does it make sense?

Close to half a million phones a day across the country, plausible for one of the largest phone markets.

Real-world check

Industry trackers put India at about 152 million smartphones shipped in 2025 (IDC). The estimate of 175 million is in the right range; a slightly longer replacement cycle, or a lower ownership share, would close the gap.

Source: IDC: India smartphone market 2025.

Separate replacement demand from new buyers

The shortcut assumes that all existing smartphone owners replace their phones at a steady rate. In a growing market, annual sales also include first-time buyers, less any users leaving the category. A more complete equation is: annual devices sold = replacements + first-time purchases + extra devices bought for work or a second SIM, if in scope.

Using the illustrative installed base of 700 million and a four-year replacement cycle gives 175 million replacements. But if the replacement cycle lengthens to five years, that falls to 140 million before first-time buyers. This single assumption can move the estimate by tens of millions.

Clarify whether you mean shipments into distribution channels or phones actually purchased by consumers. Inventory builds and sales timing can make those measures differ. In a consulting case, explain the two drivers before using an industry tracker as a validation point.
